hero.title: Turn assumptions into better decisions.
hero.intro: Gather evidence through small, ethical checks. Validation is a learning process, not a guarantee of demand or success.

lessons.title: What Validation Actually Means
lessons.summary: Choose a priority assumption and plan a claim-specific check. Your deliverable is a Validation Starting Brief.

lessons.title: Identify Your Riskiest Assumptions
lessons.summary: Expose the claims your opportunity depends on. Your deliverable is an Assumption Register with evidence status, consequences if wrong, and candidate risks.

lessons.title: Prioritise What to Test First
lessons.summary: Compare candidate assumptions, identify a feasible first learning priority, and record why it comes before other checks. Your deliverable is a Validation Priority Plan.

lessons.title: Design a Small Validation Experiment
lessons.summary: Turn your first learning priority into a bounded experiment design. Define the question, method, signals, limits, permissions and decision rule before running anything.

lessons.title: Your Validation Test Plan
lessons.summary: Organise your experiment design into a practical plan with responsibilities, permissions, evidence recording, stop conditions and a review decision. Planned work stays distinct from results.

lessons.title: Prepare Neutral Customer Conversations
lessons.summary: Prepare a conversation guide that explores recent experiences without pitching or leading the answer. Keep consent, evidence limits and anonymous notes clear.

lessons.title: Recruit Relevant Participants Ethically
lessons.summary: Plan how to invite relevant adults voluntarily, check fit without collecting unnecessary details, and record access honestly. This lesson prepares recruitment; it sends no invitations.

lessons.title: Run and Record Customer Conversations
lessons.summary: Practise a respectful customer conversation and record anonymous notes with clear source status. Use a labeled rehearsal when no permitted real conversation has occurred.

lessons.title: Separate Findings from Interpretation
lessons.summary: Organise source-backed findings, distinguish them from your explanations, and preserve contradictions and uncertainty. Rehearsal material stays practice, not customer evidence.

lessons.title: Your Customer Evidence Review
lessons.summary: Bring your customer-learning work into one bounded review. Decide what to keep, revise, investigate or pause, and hand off an honest next test without claiming demand is validated.

lessons.title: Test Your Value Proposition
lessons.summary: Turn a proposed customer benefit into one clear, testable claim. Plan a small, honest check of understanding, relevance or behaviour without treating compliments as adoption or payment.

lessons.title: Choose a Simple Test Format
lessons.summary: Compare simple formats and choose one that fits your claim, access and resources. Define what the test can reveal, what it cannot, and when to stop before building or running it.

lessons.title: Measure Behaviour Without Overclaiming
lessons.summary: Define an observable action, a clear counting rule and a bounded interpretation. Keep planned metrics separate from actual results, and distinguish prototype actions from adoption, retention or payment.

lessons.title: Explore Commitment and Payment Assumptions
lessons.summary: Distinguish interest, time commitment, stated price preference and actual payment. Plan one transparent, voluntary check with clear offer limits and honest evidence status.

lessons.title: Your Experiment Evidence Log
lessons.summary: Bring the claim, format, measurement and commitment work into one traceable log. Keep plans, actual records, rehearsal examples, deviations and interpretations clearly separated.

lessons.title: Compare Evidence with Your Assumptions
lessons.summary: Compare your original assumptions with relevant evidence, using the original review rules and honest source limits. Record supported-within-scope, weakened, mixed or unknown assessments without turning learning into launch approval.

lessons.title: Refine Your Offer and Focus
lessons.summary: Use the assumption comparison to choose a bounded refinement to your customer focus, promise or scope. Preserve the original version, explain the change and plan a new check without calling the revised offer validated.

lessons.title: Review Feasibility and Remaining Risks
lessons.summary: Review what delivery would require and what could still fail. Separate known constraints from unknowns, assign owners and checks, and keep unresolved blockers visible before any venture decision.

lessons.title: Build Your Validation Brief
lessons.summary: Bring the validation learning pack into a concise, source-linked brief. Keep findings, proposals, unknowns and unresolved risks visible before the checkpoint.

lessons.title: Validate Checkpoint: Proceed, Iterate or Pause
lessons.summary: Make a reasoned proceed, iterate or pause decision within the evidence and readiness limits. Learning completion is separate from approval to build, launch, collect money or claim demand.

children: Manually review your decision record. Go means further testing; refine or pause remain valid. Discover drafts are not imported, verified or merged automatically. Separate saving protects earlier work.
